Kidney pain after drinking alcohol ` [Highlight start] often happens because alcohol acts as a diuretic, leading to dehydration and extra strain on your kidneys [Highlight end] ` . It can also point to an underlying issue like kidney stones, a urinary tract or kidney infection, or acute kidney injury.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESawHEIkXXwQecwm2q7O1PwpfuHv3aq7UBkDz9mxKHCs5g8DoyvX6iA_5CMDwWJGqsQZHT3iVRlsmWtcRCp-O51uojZz-Lxiuj0AqW9c3tKVbm9rM1NBVEeQa1rNh7Y1uy5LG8WF9E8kchfDqS)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEScAHEIkXXg7TyvPqDCTaGdHQ-0FyLykGo3Xfwcb2qbLiMh6rLyMGi-f7YU_tb5seO1fnHWT1GX-oWO64NbU9WhiGwSgqIwkhEpmXibHgPJqNdOlavD05wFinhus_1Yd8r70S5zT522oq6xqzZXFqYk4w)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESgwEBxCJF1zaW6Nq6W-FNHk2ZvQync9eYnL8Ki1RAo1oV7uPViZDivfRRNj51vuk45Yt_dZQuYRW_3oEgpdQDzabkKoY15Hx0FRGCVbGiZadO6O9BVc-ai2UJgD5TGl56VENip0DSgRpAp3EOTXVsuP_h-Er22PsR5SqjHVCaKFtW3r32rQ)

### Common Causes

- **Dehydration:** Alcohol increases urination and dries out the body, reducing blood flow and stressing the kidneys.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEScAHEIkXXg7TyvPqDCTaGdHQ-0FyLykGo3Xfwcb2qbLiMh6rLyMGi-f7YU_tb5seO1fnHWT1GX-oWO64NbU9WhiGwSgqIwkhEpmXibHgPJqNdOlavD05wFinhus_1Yd8r70S5zT522oq6xqzZXFqYk4w)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESjwEBxCJF1wmhyXiVicc9a7EMABIn3A7vg7s6yJqNks6DnWVdToTjQWAnh407LLmqrYMWu-bv3yMVgX1vxgX77GeUE_CaU9HERE0Sf-iehP6ztYvdQZ1Z_-7dbOvEWCQik1IXZjAXKBnQya7iJB466skVXdzH_ieB2pa6gXia-ZKIdvurXOy9TLEfpme0I21NVw)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESeAHEIkXXiBHL85dYeZ94TYx6oeLsRWI8WnMTEYvNmosFTqdfEO4iEbBpdgQ_qdr7N1OZ4x0p1He5i-WVbVGsHnk3DT76VGrWGQQPA-avGMk42tb42RotCe93vVrWGqcJWrUXhgA4xc_W74TwHAC9fc19989gvY6ODQ)
- **Acute kidney injury:** Heavy or binge drinking can cause a sudden drop in kidney function as waste builds up in the blood.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESgwEBxCJF1zaW6Nq6W-FNHk2ZvQync9eYnL8Ki1RAo1oV7uPViZDivfRRNj51vuk45Yt_dZQuYRW_3oEgpdQDzabkKoY15Hx0FRGCVbGiZadO6O9BVc-ai2UJgD5TGl56VENip0DSgRpAp3EOTXVsuP_h-Er22PsR5SqjHVCaKFtW3r32rQ)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESawHEIkXXwQecwm2q7O1PwpfuHv3aq7UBkDz9mxKHCs5g8DoyvX6iA_5CMDwWJGqsQZHT3iVRlsmWtcRCp-O51uojZz-Lxiuj0AqW9c3tKVbm9rM1NBVEeQa1rNh7Y1uy5LG8WF9E8kchfDqS)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESeAHEIkXXiBHL85dYeZ94TYx6oeLsRWI8WnMTEYvNmosFTqdfEO4iEbBpdgQ_qdr7N1OZ4x0p1He5i-WVbVGsHnk3DT76VGrWGQQPA-avGMk42tb42RotCe93vVrWGqcJWrUXhgA4xc_W74TwHAC9fc19989gvY6ODQ)
- **Kidney stones:** Dehydration from alcohol can contribute to stone formation or cause existing stones to shift and trigger sharp flank or back pain.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEScAHEIkXXg7TyvPqDCTaGdHQ-0FyLykGo3Xfwcb2qbLiMh6rLyMGi-f7YU_tb5seO1fnHWT1GX-oWO64NbU9WhiGwSgqIwkhEpmXibHgPJqNdOlavD05wFinhus_1Yd8r70S5zT522oq6xqzZXFqYk4w)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESgwEBxCJF1zaW6Nq6W-FNHk2ZvQync9eYnL8Ki1RAo1oV7uPViZDivfRRNj51vuk45Yt_dZQuYRW_3oEgpdQDzabkKoY15Hx0FRGCVbGiZadO6O9BVc-ai2UJgD5TGl56VENip0DSgRpAp3EOTXVsuP_h-Er22PsR5SqjHVCaKFtW3r32rQ)
- **Urinary tract or kidney infections:** Bladder irritation or an infection that reaches the kidneys can cause flank pain, fever, or painful urination.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEScAHEIkXXg7TyvPqDCTaGdHQ-0FyLykGo3Xfwcb2qbLiMh6rLyMGi-f7YU_tb5seO1fnHWT1GX-oWO64NbU9WhiGwSgqIwkhEpmXibHgPJqNdOlavD05wFinhus_1Yd8r70S5zT522oq6xqzZXFqYk4w)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESgwEBxCJF1zaW6Nq6W-FNHk2ZvQync9eYnL8Ki1RAo1oV7uPViZDivfRRNj51vuk45Yt_dZQuYRW_3oEgpdQDzabkKoY15Hx0FRGCVbGiZadO6O9BVc-ai2UJgD5TGl56VENip0DSgRpAp3EOTXVsuP_h-Er22PsR5SqjHVCaKFtW3r32rQ)
- **Liver or pre-existing kidney issues:** Liver strain from alcohol can reduce blood flow to the kidneys, and existing kidney disease or high blood pressure can worsen after drinking.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESeAHEIkXXiBHL85dYeZ94TYx6oeLsRWI8WnMTEYvNmosFTqdfEO4iEbBpdgQ_qdr7N1OZ4x0p1He5i-WVbVGsHnk3DT76VGrWGQQPA-avGMk42tb42RotCe93vVrWGqcJWrUXhgA4xc_W74TwHAC9fc19989gvY6ODQ)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESgwEBxCJF1zaW6Nq6W-FNHk2ZvQync9eYnL8Ki1RAo1oV7uPViZDivfRRNj51vuk45Yt_dZQuYRW_3oEgpdQDzabkKoY15Hx0FRGCVbGiZadO6O9BVc-ai2UJgD5TGl56VENip0DSgRpAp3EOTXVsuP_h-Er22PsR5SqjHVCaKFtW3r32rQ)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEScAHEIkXXg7TyvPqDCTaGdHQ-0FyLykGo3Xfwcb2qbLiMh6rLyMGi-f7YU_tb5seO1fnHWT1GX-oWO64NbU9WhiGwSgqIwkhEpmXibHgPJqNdOlavD05wFinhus_1Yd8r70S5zT522oq6xqzZXFqYk4w)

### When to Seek Immediate Care
Get urgent medical attention if pain is severe or comes with warning signs such as:

- Fever or chills
- Blood in your urine or very dark urine
- Trouble urinating or very little urine output
- Swelling in your legs, ankles, or face
- Persistent nausea, vomiting, dizziness, or confusion[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESjwEBxCJF1wmhyXiVicc9a7EMABIn3A7vg7s6yJqNks6DnWVdToTjQWAnh407LLmqrYMWu-bv3yMVgX1vxgX77GeUE_CaU9HERE0Sf-iehP6ztYvdQZ1Z_-7dbOvEWCQik1IXZjAXKBnQya7iJB466skVXdzH_ieB2pa6gXia-ZKIdvurXOy9TLEfpme0I21NVw)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESgwEBxCJF1zaW6Nq6W-FNHk2ZvQync9eYnL8Ki1RAo1oV7uPViZDivfRRNj51vuk45Yt_dZQuYRW_3oEgpdQDzabkKoY15Hx0FRGCVbGiZadO6O9BVc-ai2UJgD5TGl56VENip0DSgRpAp3EOTXVsuP_h-Er22PsR5SqjHVCaKFtW3r32rQ)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESawHEIkXXwQecwm2q7O1PwpfuHv3aq7UBkDz9mxKHCs5g8DoyvX6iA_5CMDwWJGqsQZHT3iVRlsmWtcRCp-O51uojZz-Lxiuj0AqW9c3tKVbm9rM1NBVEeQa1rNh7Y1uy5LG8WF9E8kchfDqS)

### What You Can Do Right Now

- **Stop drinking alcohol** and give your body time to recover.
- **Rehydrate steadily** with water.
- **Avoid NSAIDs** (like ibuprofen or naproxen) for pain, as they can further stress the kidneys; ask a doctor or pharmacist before taking pain relievers.
- **Contact a healthcare provider** if the pain does not improve or keeps returning after you drink.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESegHEIkXXWHbUK0sJAKYAc4s2Zl5GujYOsD-dLZN_bBe0GKgivDQsUKnaF_VTktZNA8mnhAVOzESEU14gYTEq5XcT8pwHlrgMNIB6zlhzI-4AjTvQSNudn5eQ_ID9EA07hTYB-NsHQ3Z0xUiGR3YVY95HidJbCHR6jWU3)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESgwEBxCJF1zaW6Nq6W-FNHk2ZvQync9eYnL8Ki1RAo1oV7uPViZDivfRRNj51vuk45Yt_dZQuYRW_3oEgpdQDzabkKoY15Hx0FRGCVbGiZadO6O9BVc-ai2UJgD5TGl56VENip0DSgRpAp3EOTXVsuP_h-Er22PsR5SqjHVCaKFtW3r32rQ)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEScAHEIkXXg7TyvPqDCTaGdHQ-0FyLykGo3Xfwcb2qbLiMh6rLyMGi-f7YU_tb5seO1fnHWT1GX-oWO64NbU9WhiGwSgqIwkhEpmXibHgPJqNdOlavD05wFinhus_1Yd8r70S5zT522oq6xqzZXFqYk4w)[[4]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESawHEIkXXwQecwm2q7O1PwpfuHv3aq7UBkDz9mxKHCs5g8DoyvX6iA_5CMDwWJGqsQZHT3iVRlsmWtcRCp-O51uojZz-Lxiuj0AqW9c3tKVbm9rM1NBVEeQa1rNh7Y1uy5LG8WF9E8kchfDqS)[[5]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESjwEBxCJF1wmhyXiVicc9a7EMABIn3A7vg7s6yJqNks6DnWVdToTjQWAnh407LLmqrYMWu-bv3yMVgX1vxgX77GeUE_CaU9HERE0Sf-iehP6ztYvdQZ1Z_-7dbOvEWCQik1IXZjAXKBnQya7iJB466skVXdzH_ieB2pa6gXia-ZKIdvurXOy9TLEfpme0I21NVw)[[6]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESZAHEIkXX-slvCSXFZs4nXOvJooOVf-pGUPuJPc5rFcWB4dTLDvp8SDp6chiJZefjxaJSNzAjXDUj_FvzlmLyCiWq8Z1S7E8EYwGK9bMfFnP7OW3ldji-ylUiG9ccr3nGfW-WNKs)

For more details on causes and complications, see [Medical News Today](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESawHEIkXXwQecwm2q7O1PwpfuHv3aq7UBkDz9mxKHCs5g8DoyvX6iA_5CMDwWJGqsQZHT3iVRlsmWtcRCp-O51uojZz-Lxiuj0AqW9c3tKVbm9rM1NBVEeQa1rNh7Y1uy5LG8WF9E8kchfDqS), [Healthmatch](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESgwEBxCJF1zaW6Nq6W-FNHk2ZvQync9eYnL8Ki1RAo1oV7uPViZDivfRRNj51vuk45Yt_dZQuYRW_3oEgpdQDzabkKoY15Hx0FRGCVbGiZadO6O9BVc-ai2UJgD5TGl56VENip0DSgRpAp3EOTXVsuP_h-Er22PsR5SqjHVCaKFtW3r32rQ) , or [Healthline](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEScAHEIkXXg7TyvPqDCTaGdHQ-0FyLykGo3Xfwcb2qbLiMh6rLyMGi-f7YU_tb5seO1fnHWT1GX-oWO64NbU9WhiGwSgqIwkhEpmXibHgPJqNdOlavD05wFinhus_1Yd8r70S5zT522oq6xqzZXFqYk4w).[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESawHEIkXXwQecwm2q7O1PwpfuHv3aq7UBkDz9mxKHCs5g8DoyvX6iA_5CMDwWJGqsQZHT3iVRlsmWtcRCp-O51uojZz-Lxiuj0AqW9c3tKVbm9rM1NBVEeQa1rNh7Y1uy5LG8WF9E8kchfDqS)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESgwEBxCJF1zaW6Nq6W-FNHk2ZvQync9eYnL8Ki1RAo1oV7uPViZDivfRRNj51vuk45Yt_dZQuYRW_3oEgpdQDzabkKoY15Hx0FRGCVbGiZadO6O9BVc-ai2UJgD5TGl56VENip0DSgRpAp3EOTXVsuP_h-Er22PsR5SqjHVCaKFtW3r32rQ)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEScAHEIkXXg7TyvPqDCTaGdHQ-0FyLykGo3Xfwcb2qbLiMh6rLyMGi-f7YU_tb5seO1fnHWT1GX-oWO64NbU9WhiGwSgqIwkhEpmXibHgPJqNdOlavD05wFinhus_1Yd8r70S5zT522oq6xqzZXFqYk4w)To help me give more relevant information, are you asking for yourself or someone else, and what **symptoms** (such as fever, nausea, or changes in urination) are present alongside the **pain**?

items.title: Common Causes
items.text: Dehydration: Alcohol increases urination and dries out the body, reducing blood flow and stressing the kidneys. Acute kidney injury: Heavy or binge drinking can cause a sudden drop in kidney function as waste builds up in the blood. Kidney stones: Dehydration from alcohol can contribute to stone formation or cause existing stones to shift and trigger sharp flank or back pain. Urinary tract or kidney infections: Bladder irritation or an infection that reaches the kidneys can cause flank pain, fever, or painful urination. Liver or pre-existing kidney issues: Liver strain from alcohol can reduce blood flow to the kidneys, and existing kidney disease or high blood pressure can worsen after drinking.

items.text: Stop drinking alcohol and give your body time to recover. Rehydrate steadily with water. Avoid NSAIDs (like ibuprofen or naproxen) for pain, as they can further stress the kidneys; ask a doctor or pharmacist before taking pain relievers. Contact a healthcare provider if the pain does not improve or keeps returning after you drink.
